cards.front: What is the key assumption of the particle model in mechanics?
cards.back: Size and shape are ignored, so all forces act through a single point.

options.text: Size and shape are ignored, so all forces act through a single point.
options.explanation: The particle model treats an object as having mass but negligible dimensions, allowing every force to be considered as acting through one point and ignoring rotational effects.

options.text: Mass and weight are equal, so all forces act through the centre of mass.
options.explanation: Mass and weight are different physical quantities, and the particle model does not require forces to act through the centre of mass. It ignores size and shape and uses a single point.

options.text: Size and shape are important, so all forces act through a single point.
options.explanation: Treating size and shape as important contradicts the particle assumption, which removes dimensions from the model. The correct simplification is to ignore them and make forces act through one point.

options.text: Size and shape are ignored, so all forces act along a single line.
options.explanation: A particle model specifies one point of action, not merely one line. Confusing these ideas can lead to incorrect torque reasoning; the correct assumption ignores size and shape.
